facts.statement: Term insurance pays a death benefit only if the insured dies during the term.
facts.quote: pays a death benefit only if you die in that term

items.stem: A client buys a standard 20-year level term life policy at age 40 and is still alive when the term ends at age 60. What does the policy pay?
options: The face amount, as a living benefit
The cash value built up over 20 years
A refund of all premiums paid
Nothing, because no death occurred during the term
items.explanation: Per NJ DOBI, Consumer Information: Life Insurance, term insurance pays a death benefit only if the insured dies during the term, and it does not build cash value.

facts.statement: Term insurance generally has lower premiums in the early years but builds no cash value.
facts.quote: Term insurance generally has lower premiums in the early years, but does not build up cash values that you can use in the future.

items.stem: Compared with permanent life insurance, term insurance generally has:
options: Lower early premiums and no cash value
Higher early premiums and a growing cash value
Lower early premiums and a guaranteed cash value
Higher early premiums and no cash value
items.explanation: Per NJ DOBI, Consumer Information: Life Insurance, term insurance generally has lower premiums in the early years and does not build up cash values.

facts.statement: Most term policies can be renewed for further terms even if health has changed, but premiums may rise at each renewal.
facts.quote: You can renew most term insurance policies for one or more terms even if your health has changed. Each time you renew the policy for a new term, premiums may be higher.

items.stem: A client's renewable 10-year term policy is ending, and she has developed heart disease since buying it. If she renews for another term, she can expect:
options: Coverage to continue, likely at a higher premium
To be declined, because her health has changed
To keep the same premium as her first term
To have the face amount reduced to her cash value
items.explanation: Per the NAIC Life Insurance Buyer's Guide, most term policies can be renewed for one or more terms even if health has changed, and premiums may be higher at each renewal.

facts.statement: Many term policies can be converted to a cash value policy during a conversion period even if the insured is not in good health; the new premium will be higher.
facts.quote: You may be able to trade many term insurance policies for a cash value policy during a conversion period - even if you are not in good health.

items.stem: A client with a convertible term policy has been diagnosed with diabetes and wants permanent coverage. Within the conversion period, he can generally:
options: Convert it if he first passes a medical exam
Exchange it for a cash value policy without proving good health
Convert it, keeping the same premium he pays for term
Exchange it for a policy with a higher face amount at term rates
items.explanation: Per the NAIC Life Insurance Buyer's Guide, many term policies can be traded for a cash value policy during a conversion period even if the insured is not in good health, though the new premium will be higher than the term premium.

facts.statement: Term insurance generally offers the largest insurance protection for the premium dollar.
facts.quote: Term insurance generally offers the largest insurance protection for your premium dollar.

items.stem: A young parent on a tight budget needs the largest possible death benefit for the next 20 years. Which type of policy generally provides the most coverage per premium dollar?
options: Whole life
Universal life
Term life
Variable life
items.explanation: Per the NAIC Life Insurance Buyer's Guide, term insurance generally offers the largest insurance protection for your premium dollar.
